Shahadat Parvez And 3 Others vs Union Of India And 3 Others
on 12 January, 2023
Bench: Sunita Agarwal, Vipin Chandra Dixit
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Case :- Writ - C No. - 37461 of 2022
Petitioner :- Shahadat Parvez And 3 Others

Respondent :- Union Of India And 3 Others
Counsel for Petitioner :- Rahul Kumar Tyagi

Counsel for Respondent :- A.S.G.I.,C.S.C.,Pranjal Mehrotra Hon'ble Mrs. Sunita Agarwal,J.
Hon'ble Vipin Chandra Dixit,J.
Heard learned counsel for the petitioners.
Sri Pranjal Mehrotra, learned Advocate has put in appearance on behalf of respondents no. 1 and 2.

The petitioners herein claim to be the heirs and legal representatives of Mr. Ashraf son of Mr. Asgar in whose name rehabilitation and resettlement award was passed by the Land Acquisition Officer on 13.07.2016 in accordance with the provisions of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
In the writ petition, it is sought to be submitted that the name of the petitioners and their mother were collectively recorded in the revenue records as co-sharers and the entry in the Khatauni 1424-1429 fasli based on the order dated 12.07.2017 passed by Tehsildar has been appended as Annexure No. '1' to the writ petition.

sentences.text: It is sought to be submitted by the learned counsel for the petitioners that the father of the petitioners had died before publication of the acquisition notification but the said statement made during the course of argument is not supported by any averment in the writ petition.
The date of death of the father of the petitioners and the dates of notifications have not been disclosed in the writ petition.
The submissions made without any statement with that regard in the writ petition are not entertainable, being off the record.

It is an admitted fact of the matter that resettlement and rehabilitation award dated 13.07.2016 was passed in the name of the father of the petitioners and the total amount of Rs. 5,50,000/-
determined therein had been received by the mother of the petitioners after the death of her husband.

In none of the paragraphs of the writ petition, it is disclosed the the petitioners have ever laid their claim before the competent authority/Land Acquisition Officer for declaration of rehabilitation and resettlement award separately in their names, after the death of their father.

The contention of the learned counsel for the petitioners that the petitioners being the co-sharers of the acquired land were entitled for rehabilitation and resettlement grant separately having their individual right in the property in question as co-owner at the time of acquisition, therefore, cannot be entertained.
At this stage, learned counsel for the petitioners prays to withdraw the present petition to approach the competent authority with correct and complete details.
In view of above, the writ petition is dismissed as withdrawn with liberty to the petitioners to approach the appropriate authority for redressal of their grievances.
